faq.q: Do I need an account to play PokeRogue?
faq.a: Yes. The original game opens an account screen first, so this is an account-based game rather than a guest demo. Sign-in, registration and saves are managed by pokerogue.net, not by this site.

faq.q: Can I play PokeRogue on my phone?
faq.a: Start at pokerogue.net in your mobile browser. A home-screen shortcut opens the same web game, while the community offline app is a separate wrapper. We did not test a physical phone, so check the mobile guide before installing anything.

faq.q: Should I accept the Dark Deal?
faq.a: Refuse if your run cannot survive losing an essential team member. Accepting removes a randomly selected Pokémon and opens a catchable boss fight, in return for five Rogue Balls.

faq.q: Trash to Treasure: dig or investigate?
faq.a: Digging avoids the fight but makes shop items and rerolls cost 2.5 times as much for the rest of the run. Investigating risks a Garbodor boss battle and lets you choose a reward afterward.

faq.q: Will my saves move between the browser and the offline app?
faq.a: The community wiki says data can transfer from online to offline, but not back. Treat an offline run as a separate commitment and keep a backup through the supported export process.

faq.q: Is this the same game as PokeBonk?
faq.a: No. PokeRogue is a turn-based Pokémon roguelite by the Pagefault Games project; PokeBonk and other similarly named Pokémon projects are different games with their own pages.

faq.q: Can I catch Eternatus on my first Classic clear?
faq.a: Only if you have already unlocked every other starter. Ordinary Classic checks your starter collection before ball strength or the remaining boss shields.
